concepts.title: Elections and Democracy: Why Free and Fair Elections Matter

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Elections and Democracy: Why Free and Fair Elections Matter' refers to.
questions.a: Modern democracy runs through elections: they convert citizens' preferences into a governing body, let people dismiss rulers peacefully, and force parties to court public opinion. Elections qualify as democratic only when they are free -- no coercion or fear -- and fair -- impartially conducted with equal weight for each vote.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Elections and Democracy: Why Free and Fair Elections Matter'.
questions.a: Elections are democracy's gearbox -- free choice inside a fair procedure turns votes into government.

concepts.title: Election Commission of India: The Independent Referee

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Election Commission of India: The Independent Referee' refers to.
questions.a: The Election Commission of India supervises and controls the entire electoral process -- preparing rolls, scheduling polls, enforcing the model code of conduct, and certifying results. Its independence comes from constitutional protection: Commissioners can be removed only like judges of the Supreme Court, and its spending is charged on the Consolidated Fund.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Election Commission of India: The Independent Referee'.
questions.a: One referee above all players -- the Commission's independence is what keeps political contests honest.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Election Commission of India: The Independent Referee' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: First Past the Post and Proportional Representation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'First Past the Post and Proportional Representation' refers to.
questions.a: Two great families of electoral systems exist. First past the post divides the country into single-member constituencies and elects whoever tops the count there -- simple and area-anchored, but it can hand large seats to a party with a modest vote share. Proportional representation allocates seats in proportion to votes, using party lists or transferable votes -- fairer in shares, weaker in constituency bonds.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'First Past the Post and Proportional Representation'.
questions.a: Winner-takes-all by area, or seats-by-share -- each system trades simplicity against proportionality.

concepts.title: Reservation of Constituencies and Universal Franchise

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Reservation of Constituencies and Universal Franchise' refers to.
questions.a: The Constitution adopted universal adult franchise at once, making every adult a voter regardless of wealth, gender or education. To open legislatures to historically excluded groups, it reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Tribes in proportion to population, while reserving a third of local-body seats for women -- representation as inclusion, not just counting.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Reservation of Constituencies and Universal Franchise'.
questions.a: One person one vote one value -- plus reserved seats so the excluded do not stay outside the house.
